# kube-agents — Build Ledger

**This file is the harness's memory across sessions and days. Every run reads it first** — before
the roadmap, before the code — to learn where the build is, and updates it before stopping. Context
does not survive a session; this file does. It is the single source of truth for build progress —
not chat history, not git log alone.

- **Source of truth for _what_ to build:** `docs/design/` (01–09). Never contradict a spec; if a
  spec is genuinely silent, pick the simplest option consistent with the invariants, implement it,
  and record it under **Decisions & deviations** below.
- **Source of truth for _how_ to build:** `docs/design/07-implementation-roadmap.md` (phases,
  acceptance, verification loop §5) + `.claude/harness/PROTOCOL.md` (the state machine) +
  `.claude/harness/invariants.md` (the pre-merge gate).
- **Source of truth for _whether it is proven_:** `docs/design/09-verification-and-validation.md` —
  every check has a stable ID (`V-<SUITE>-<nnn>`), a level (L0–L4), and a gate class. The harness
  runs checks **by ID**; it does not invent tests.
- **Project-specific values** (paths, clusters, commands, remotes, thresholds):
  `.claude/harness/binding.md`. **Durable lessons:** `.claude/harness/LESSONS.md`.
- **How the loop works:** `.claude/skills/harness-{run,verify,milestone,improve}/SKILL.md`.

**State fields in this file, and what each is for:**

| Section | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **Status** | Current phase, current unit, autonomy, targets, and any active halt. Read at ORIENT before anything else |
| **Phase progress** | One row per phase: status, PR, outcome. `harness-milestone` closes a row and opens the next |
| **Verification results — by check ID** | The 09 §9.4 evidence record, one row per check run: `check_id, level, target, result, evidence_ref`. **A `pass` with no `evidence_ref` is recorded as `skipped`.** The rows live in `verification/results.csv`; this section is the pointer and the rules |
| **Deferrals** | Every check not run, with a **named external blocker**, an owner, and a promotion condition. Never a pass. A BLOCKING-ALWAYS check may never appear here |
| **Metrics snapshot** | SELF-IMPROVEMENT §6 — escape rate, rework, halts, open lessons, deferrals, coverage, cycle time. Recorded at each milestone; inputs to the improvement pass, never targets |
| **Lessons opened / closed** | Pointer into `.claude/harness/LESSONS.md`. An open lesson is a defect in the harness and appears in every orientation |
| **History** | What moved to `archive/LEDGER-phases-0-7.md` and to `verification/results.csv`, and why. Phases 0–7 progress, the suite-level Verification log, the Definition of Done, and the Outer-loop install record are all there, verbatim |
| **Decisions & deviations** | Choices the specs did not dictate, with rationale. What a reviewer reads to understand the build. Phase 8 here, Phases 0–7 in the archive |
| **Blockers** | Anything halting autonomous progress. **A halt is cleared by a human**, never by the harness |

**This file is deliberately not prettier-formatted** (`.prettierignore`). Prettier pads every table
cell out to its column's widest, which cost 64% of the file — 446 KB in 414 lines, too big for one
`Read` of the file the protocol says to read first. Write table rows with single spaces around the
pipes; nothing will re-pad them.

| Current phase | **Phase 9 — The Action Broker, dark** (07 §2), entered 2026-07-27 when the Phase 8 milestone closed. Build the **entire** safety machinery — broker, envelope, risk classifier, journal, undo plan, brake — and exercise it end to end **with no write authority anywhere**: actor ServiceAccounts created but bound to **empty** roles, every action dry-run, every `ActionRecord` a would-have-executed. That shape is the point, not caution: the hardest and most novel code in the build lands, gets reviewed and gets tested against real clusters while the worst possible bug is still a no-op, which turns Phase 10 into a permission change rather than a leap. Ten tasks, five of them load-bearing (T2 envelope + scope-derived-from-caller, T3 classifier + `ChangePolicy` that may only tighten, T4 undo-plan generation whose "cannot generate" path **reclassifies the action as gated**, T6 the brake, which must work through `kubectl` with inference down, T9 the consolidated gate). **PLAN landed 2026-07-27: [`docs/build/phase-9.md`](phase-9.md)** — survey (the pipeline is greenfield: five CRDs, a second binary, a second image, a second Deployment per CR, none of which exist), the Accept→check binding, the ten-unit breakdown, deferrals, and IMPLEMENT notes. It resolves **four planning defects** before any code: **(1)** 07 §2's "bound to **empty** roles" is literally incompatible with journalling — 06 §2.2.1's broker operations grant is what lets the broker authenticate (step 1), read the brake (step 5) and write the journal (step 11), and omitting it "does not fail safe — it bricks the tier"; so "empty" means empty of _tenant_ authority and Accept (e)'s sweep becomes the two-sided **V-BRK-013** assertion. **(2)** V-BRK/V-REV/V-ISO are **BLOCKING-ALWAYS and may not be deferred** (09 §9.6), yet ~11 of their checks need a real mutation that dark mode forbids — resolved by one code path and two RBAC profiles, with a test-only tenant overlay confined to `dev/` by a new `invariants-gate.py` check, rather than by shipping checks that cannot fail (V-MET-014). **(3)** V-BRK-003 needs an audit-log stream GKE only exposes through Cloud Logging, with Data Access logs off by default — the reconciler takes a pluggable audit source and P9-T1 opens with the probe. **(4)** Accept (a)–(e) does not cover the ratchet: V-RUN (14) and V-ISO-001/002/006 are 17 required checks no Accept bullet names, so the gate runs the ratchet and Accept is the subset 07 chose to print. _Prior phase:_ **Phase 8 — Contain the pod, close the boundary, make the install real**, ✅ merged via [#30](https://github.com/adamparco/kube-agents/pull/30); it added no imperative capability, it removed the reasons starting would be unsafe. Breakdown and evidence: `docs/build/phase-8.md`, the Phase progress row below, and [`archive/LEDGER-phases-0-7.md`](archive/LEDGER-phases-0-7.md) §Status for everything before it. |
| Current task | **P9-T8b-4b-ii-1 done 2026-07-30 — a permission boundary is now an answer, not a crash.** T8b-4b-i filed one finding as 4b-ii's _first order of business_: an RBAC denial inside step 3 surfaced as a `500 internal-error` with a stack trace, and the choice between typing the refusal and granting the actor a read was flagged as a real design question. It is answered, and answering it split the unit. **`agent-identity.yaml.template` settles the grant**: Phase 9's actor authority is the 06 §2.2.1 broker-operations grant and nothing else, because binding a cloud-write credential now would hand the actor months of authority ahead of the controls meant to bound it (P10-T1 owns that). So the actor genuinely cannot read a tenant object, and 06 §4.4's fail-closed table already required a refusal — it just did not say which. **There are two, and they differ by whether retrying could ever help.** An API-server fault may succeed a minute later: `503 snapshot-failed`, with a Retry-After. An RBAC denial will not: `403 target-forbidden`, with none — `Refusal.RetryAfterSeconds`'s own comment says zero is the right answer for every authorization refusal, and this was the site not honouring it. **The part that made it more than a status code**: `Journal` and `SecurityEvent` are fields _on_ the `Refusal`, so an untyped error meant the envelope's disposition was recorded **nowhere** — an agent enumerating what it may touch left no trace, which is the opposite of what 06 §4.1's per-reason table exists to guarantee. The forbidden arm therefore journals and deliberately does **not** alarm: 03 §6's events are identity violations, `forbidden-caller` remains that case, and an alarm on every shadow-mode action is an alarm that gets muted. **V-BRK-031 at L1 and L2**, `¬` on the discrimination rather than the happy arm (a check asserting only "step 3 refuses" passes on an implementation answering 403 for everything, which is exactly how this gets written wrong), **8/8 mutants caught**, and at L2 a real API server denied the real shipped actor and the broker answered `403 target-forbidden` where the run three days ago answered `500`. `broker-auth-l2.sh` is 14 PASS / 0 FAIL, rc 0, twice. **Why 4b-ii-2 is a separate unit**: with the shipped grant no envelope reaches step 4, so the `DryRun` population is _empty_, and phase-9.md's own argument against a vacuous V-REV-001 applies to the shadow instance as much as the executed one. The soak needs planning defect 2's **read-only** tenant overlay — not a weakening, since invariant 7's allow-list is `get`/`list`/`watch` and read verbs are explicitly not authority. Next: **T8b-4b-ii-2**, the overlay plus guard 1 plus the soak. |

| Last updated | 2026-07-30 — **P9-T9a checkpointed.** **V-MET-007** recorded `pass` at L0, **retracting the 2026-07-27 finding on the same ID**; no new check ID was allocated, and 09 §6 is untouched. Gate: L0 chain clean · `make validate` pass · spec-ids OK (248 check IDs, unchanged) · invariants-gate 21/21 · sweep **15/15** caught. Two things are worth carrying forward. The matcher is **calibrated against GitHub rather than against a reading of GitHub**: the whole answer turns on whether a leading `**/` may match zero directories, so the test replays PR #33 (gate did not fire) and PR #79 (it did) against the filter as it stood, and a misreading of `**` in either direction flips one of them. And the check is **one-directional on purpose** — it proves a glob missing, never unnecessary, and `- "**"` would satisfy it; over-triggering costs CI minutes, under-triggering costs a review, so the rule only pushes where being wrong is cheap. **Caught en route by a gate, not by a reader:** the first draft enumerated the repo with a bare `git ls-files`, and invariants-gate refused it under LSN-050 — `ls-files` without `--others` lists the index, so the check would have been blind to precisely the new, never-reviewed file it exists to find. That is the defect it is about, one level up, and a mechanized lesson found it in seconds. |

| **Merge policy (set by user 2026-07-24):** phase PRs are **auto-merged once the pre-merge gate is |
| green** (invariants + the load-bearing suites passing at L2), then the build continues — no wait for |
| manual merge. Auto-merge is gated, not blind: any halt condition below blocks the merge and surfaces |
| instead. **Base/target = `main`** — PR #1 consolidated design + Phase 0 onto `main` (`11d95fd`), so |
| future phase branches base on `main` and PR → `main`. (Product runtime GitOps review is unaffected — |
| that is a separate, RBAC/VAP-enforced property of the built system.) |

**Load-bearing halt conditions (stop and surface, do NOT merge or auto-advance):**

1. A **security negative test** (03 §11) fails — read-only, per-tier scope, attenuation, no break-glass.
2. A **failure-isolation chaos test** (05 §8) fails.
3. An **invariant** (`.claude/harness/invariants.md`) would be violated by the change.
4. A destructive test is about to run against a context that is not an anchored **`gke-scratch-*`**.
5. A spec conflict with no simplest-option resolution.

The assembly owns no policy — only the ORDER, the type conversions between one package's output and the next one's input, and the record of which steps ran, because a rule reimplemented here would be a second opinion about a question already answered and the second opinion is the one that drifts. **`broker.StepTrace` enforces 03 §4.1 rather than reporting it**: `Run` refuses a step that is not the immediate successor of the last one recorded, seals on the first refusal or fault, and is the only way the pipeline advances — so "six of these steps are not skippable by any caller" is an error returned at the moment it is attempted. **V-BRK-011 and V-BRK-014 both pass at L1.** V-BRK-014 is BLOCKING-ALWAYS, has a fault case at every one of the eleven steps, derives its coverage from `FirstStep..LastStep` rather than counting ([[LSN-036]]), asserts that the **world** stopped and not merely the trace, and carries a mandatory negative control (09 §6 marks it `¬`) that was itself mutation-tested. Every decision follows from one asymmetry the classifier already has: it takes the **max** over sources, so *every* way of failing to see a policy is a loosening and none of them has a symmetric failure — which makes "classify against what we have" and "classify against nothing" the same bug at different sizes. Hence `Binds` returns false for a nil policy rather than treating it as fleet-wide; hence an ill-formed selector scope is checked for **every** policy before asking whether it binds, since `scope.Contains` stops at the first level a scope does not narrow and an entry with an empty level above a non-empty one would match a cluster of that name in *every* project; hence one bad rule refuses the **whole** snapshot naming the policy rather than skipping the rule. **The deferral's own name was the wrong design.** It was written as "the `ChangePolicy` informer", and this repo has already written down why a cache is the wrong shape here — `broker.MaxFreezeStaleness`: "a watch that silently stopped delivering is not an error at all — the informer's List succeeds, the cache answers instantly, and every answer is from before the incident started." A cache-backed source needs a freshness signal the cache cannot provide, and every way of building one ends in a periodic read; at that point the cache buys latency, not correctness. So it polls (`DefaultRefreshInterval` 10s, three polls inside a 30s `MaxPolicyStaleness` that deliberately mirrors the freeze), freshness is true by construction, and a tightening costs one interval. The seam in the pipeline is `Config.Classifier ClassifierSource` — was a fixed `*classify.Classifier`, which made `kubectl apply -f tighten.yaml` a no-op until restart — and when `Current()` errors, step 4 returns **503 `policy-unavailable`**, journalled and flagged as a security event, rather than falling back to the code floor, because that fallback is a silent downgrade of every policy in the cluster arriving exactly when the cluster is unhealthy. **The envtest run found a design flaw the unit tests could not.** The first draft handled every failed poll identically — retain the last good snapshot, age out at 30s. Against a real API server, `TestALoweringPolicyStoredInTheClusterCannotTakeEffect` failed: a policy that will not load is **not transient**, it will fail every poll until a human edits the object, so aging it out means 30 seconds of classifying against a set the broker already knows is wrong and the operator learns from a delayed timeout instead of at once. Split: a **read** failure retains and ages, a **load** failure discards and refuses immediately. **V-GAT-009 re-recorded at L1 over the live loader**, negative control mandatory (09 §6 marks it `¬`) and mutation-verified on both the unit and envtest sides; **its L2 instance stays open**. **T7c-2b is HALTED** — 05 §1.3 mandates `POST /v1alpha1/actions/{actionId}/replay` while V-BRK-021, BLOCKING-ALWAYS, asserts "one listening port, one mutating route", a phrase its cited source 03 §4.1 does not contain. See Blockers. **T7c-3b done 2026-07-28** ([#54](https://github.com/adamparco/kube-agents/pull/54), `9f326ff`) — **the undo planner can ask a real cluster what points at an object, and V-REV-010 is green at L2.** `refindex.Source` (the production `undo.ReferenceIndex`) enumerates the target's scope from live discovery — `ServerPreferredNamespacedResources` for a namespaced target, `ServerGroupsAndResources` for a cluster-scoped one — lists each kind as `PartialObjectMetadata` so a scan does not pull whole bodies, and reports the objects whose `ownerReferences` carry the target's **UID**. **The unit's central decision is what counts as a reference, and it goes in the loosening direction, so the argument is in the package doc where someone would undo it.** 06 §4.3.1 says "every ownerReference, PVC binding, and external reference pointing at **the old one**": what a recreate destroys is the UID, so a UID-valued reference dangles and a **by-name** reference is *repaired* by the recreate. Reporting every reference-shaped field would read as extra safety and is the opposite — on a real cluster nearly every object is named by something, so it would downgrade nearly every `delete` to `none` and make the `recreate` strategy dead code, and a gate that always fires is indistinguishable from no gate. The residual is written down rather than left to be rediscovered: a UID-valued field outside `ownerReferences` (only `PV.spec.claimRef.uid` in core Kubernetes, unreachable because PV/PVC are on `undo.nonRecreatableKinds` and short-circuit before the index is consulted) and references held outside the cluster, which no in-cluster scan can see. The **negative control is that boundary**, not a formality: a Pod mounting the target ConfigMap by name must change nothing. **The two adapters written this week fail in opposite directions on purpose.** `livestate.Source` skips a kind it cannot list; `refindex.Source` refuses the entire scan, `apierrors.IsForbidden` getting its own message naming the grant. The direction is set by what a partial answer means to the caller: a smaller blast-radius denominator makes every fraction larger and the abort MORE likely, whereas an empty reference slice reads as "nothing points at it, the recreate is safe" — and `undo.ReferenceIndex`'s own doc comment already says those two answers must never be conflated. Mutation-tested: turning the Forbidden branch into a `continue` reddens both the unlistable-kind test and the negative control. **`bodystore.Journal`** is the production `execute.BodyStore`. It calls `journal.SnapshotKey` (extracted this unit from `snapshot.go`, which had the format string inline) rather than re-deriving the layout, and it returns the **sink's** digest unaltered — [[LSN-034]] applied directly, since `execute.capture` compares that digest against its own and a store that hashed the bytes it was handed would be handing back a value the caller is about to compare with itself. Mutation-tested through the real `execute.CaptureAll`. **V-REV-010 allocated in 09 §6.3** (`L1, L2`, weight 9, `¬`): no existing row claimed the property, and V-REV-004's round-trip corpus supplies its own reference index, so it proves the recreate *step* is right for objects already stipulated recreatable — whether *this* object is one of those was unasserted at every level. Mapped onto `06§10#36`, whose bullet says "delete of a **reconstructable** object → recreate" and never tested the qualifier. **What makes it L2 is that the harm is demonstrated, not described.** envtest runs no kube-controller-manager, so an `ownerReference` there is an annotation with no consequences and 06 §4.3.1's premise is untestable below L2. On `gke-scratch-kube-agents-dev` the probe deletes the owner, polls a **real garbage collector** destroying the dependent, recreates the owner from its snapshot (new UID `31cf721c…`, was `31fc32ed…`) and shows the dependent stays gone — the exact state a `recreate` plan would have reported as a completed undo. The probe fails loudly rather than skipping if no GC is observed, because "the dependent survived" would otherwise read as the downgrade being unnecessary. **Two findings, neither failure-driven, both deferred with named owners rather than folded in.** A full-surface scan of one namespace on a 57-kind cluster takes **9.1 s**, sequential and O(kinds), and it sits in the request path at pipeline step 4 — a CRD-heavy cluster is worse and nothing measures it. And **no production `journal.BlobSink` exists anywhere in the tree**: the interface has been there since T1, `cmd/broker` passes `nil`, and `bodystore.Journal` is now complete with nothing to talk to — so any pre-state over 1 MiB refuses the action outright, which is 03 §6's fail-closed direction and an availability cost that is invisible until someone patches a large ConfigMap. A real sink needs a bucket, a GSA through Workload Identity and a lifecycle policy matching 06 §4.3's TTLs, which is a provisioning unit, not an adapter unit. **Both `test/l2/` wrappers now pin `go test -run` to their own tests** — one package, two checks, and without the filter a V-REV-010 red would be reported as V-GAT-022 failing. The vacuity guard that `-run` introduces (a typo selects nothing and exits 0) was verified by running a deliberately-typo'd copy of the script. **Explicit non-claim:** `cmd/broker` still installs `UnavailablePipeline{}`; [[LSN-007]] stands until **T7c-3d**. **T7c-3c-i done 2026-07-28** ([#56](https://github.com/adamparco/kube-agents/pull/56), `d988fdf`) — the broker can now ask a real cluster whether an action actually worked, and V-PRO-027 is green at L1 and L2.** `internal/broker/probe` is the production `verify.Prober`: eight methods behind the eight rows of the 04 §5.1 table. **The failure direction is per-method, and uniformity would be the bug** — that is the package's central argument and it is written into its doc. A restart count whose workload selector will not resolve **errors**, because zero restarts is the *passing* answer for the Deployment row, so a count that was never counted verifies every rollout. A Service with no ready endpoint returns **zero and no error**, because the predicate reads zero as Pending and erroring would make every not-yet-ready Service a probe failure instead of a wait. An absent capability returns **`ErrProbeUnsupported`**, which becomes Indeterminate and, at the settle deadline, a rollback — expensive, and the correct direction. **The uid pin is the clause with no cheaper substitute:** a settle window is minutes long, and inside it an object can be deleted and recreated at the same name by a human, a reconciler, or the garbage collector; the replacement is usually *healthy*, so every other probe reports the action as verified and only `metadata.uid` distinguishes them. **The LimitRange probe has two legs** for the same reason `connectivityPredicate` does — a LimitRange has no status, so enforcement can only be observed by asking admission, and "submit something illegal and watch it be rejected" has many possible authors (PSA, a webhook, a quota, an RBAC 403); a compliant pod and a violating pod, both `DryRunAll`, both otherwise identical, make the differentiator a fact this function controls rather than the wording of an error. **`ProviderState` makes no cloud API call, deliberately**: Config Connector already writes the provider's answer into the CR's status, so the broker verifies a cloud change with no cloud credential — and `observedGeneration` is what keeps it from being a status echo. **The L1 suite passed on its first run, which proves nothing**, so a **10-mutation sweep** was run before the evidence was written; all 10 were killed and the sweep exposed the one missing negative control, the SAR `evaluationError` path, staged through `client/interceptor` because no real API server produces one on demand. **L2 exists because envtest runs an API server and no controllers** — every status the L1 suite reads is one the L1 suite wrote. On `gke-scratch-kube-agents-dev`: a real deployment controller that has not converged (04 §5.1's opening sentence as an assertion — the write returned success and the verdict is Pending), a **real kubelet** restarting `flapper` (busybox `sleep 20; exit 7`, the rolled-out-then-fell-over shape) while `steady` next door stays at zero *at the same moment*, a real endpoint-slice controller publishing 2, GKE's real authorizer chain answering both directions, and a real deletion issuing a genuinely new uid. **The negative control's headline is only meaningful there**: in a PSA-`restricted` namespace both dry-run legs are refused, so the probe must report not-observed — and the one-leg mutation claims enforcement, as demonstrated. **Three findings, none failure-driven, none fixed here (PROTOCOL §10.1):** the **connectivity prober is unwired** and needs a probe workload with its own RBAC and blast-radius argument, so it is a provisioning unit (Deferrals); a **route-less Gateway is a false positive** that errors, holds Pending and is rolled back, whose honest fix is to change the 04 §5.1 row from an endpoint count to `Accepted`/`Programmed`; and `clusterNodeCounts` **cannot catch a node that never registered** because its denominator is the registered set. **Explicit non-claim:** `cmd/broker` still installs `UnavailablePipeline{}`; [[LSN-007]] stands until P9-T7c-3d. **T7c-3c-ii-a done 2026-07-28** ([#57](https://github.com/adamparco/kube-agents/pull/57), `5baabcf`) —  an undo plan can now actually be replayed, and V-REV-011 is green at L1 and L2.** `internal/broker/rollback` is the production `verify.Rollbacker`: until this unit, rung 3 of the 04 §5.1 ladder was an interface with no implementation, and `06§10#36`'s "and then **actually replayed**" had no check behind it — V-REV-004 generates and validates plans and never runs one. **The package is built on the three promises `internal/broker/undo` makes to a replayer that did not exist, and writing it turned one of them out to be false** (the Secret finding, below). **`Create` lives on `execute.ClientApplier` and deliberately not on the `Applier` interface**: a recreate step carries no uid precondition — the uid died with the object — so its only protection against restoring a snapshot on top of a stranger who took the name is that a create returns `AlreadyExists`; no execution path needs `Create`, since an agent's `create` verb goes through Apply like every other write because SSA is what carries field-manager attribution, so widening the shared interface would have grown dead bodies on two unrelated fakes. A narrow `Writer` interface sits beside its one consumer with `var _ Writer = (*execute.ClientApplier)(nil)` to stop the two drifting. **`agentIdentity` is a per-call argument, not constructor state** — the replayer derives its FIELD MANAGER from it and V-BRK-019 fixes that manager at `kube-agents/<tier>/<scope>`, so an implementation constructed once with a static identity writes the right manager until the process serves a second agent and the wrong one silently thereafter; `verify.Rollbacker` was widened to match and both fakes now ASSERT the identity they were handed. **A real production bug the tests found and this unit fixes:** `encoding/json` decodes every JSON number to `float64` and `unstructured.NestedInt64` reports a `float64` as **absent** rather than as the wrong type, so the scale step would have refused every plan it was handed while blaming the planner for omitting a `spec.replicas` that was right there in the bytes. **[[LSN-040]] closed in one place:** `ValidateReplayable`'s default arm used to assert something about "the replayer" that had not been written; the op set is now single-sourced as `undo.ReplayableOps()`, consumed by the validator and by the test that iterates it. **L1: 28 tests, 33 subtests, and a 14-mutation sweep, all 14 caught.** **What makes the L2 half necessary is the word "pre-state"** — at L1 a successful replay means a field changed, which is the *request* that would produce the pre-state, not the pre-state; the pre-state of a scaled-down Deployment is running pods, and only a real controller and a real kubelet put them back. On `gke-scratch-kube-agents-dev` the probe drains a two-replica Deployment to zero, replays, and asserts two READY replicas restored by controllers it never spoke to — paired with a bystander's annotation that must SURVIVE, since applying the whole snapshot would satisfy "the replicas are back" while silently undoing every unrelated change. The recreate clause gets a real deletion under Foreground propagation with the real GC reaping the ReplicaSets, and the refusal at a taken name gets its **counterfactual measured rather than argued**: same body, same manager, Apply instead of Create, on a fourth object — apply raised an SSA **conflict**, neither the `AlreadyExists` the recreate relies on nor any report that the object is gone, and a conflict is a statement about field ownership that would simply be absent if the stranger left those fields unset. **Three fixture bugs were caught by the control legs, not by the refusal legs** — plans missing `Validated: true` were refused by `ValidateReplayable` so every "refusal" passed on the wrong refusal; `undo.Sanitize`'s second argument is `isStatusTarget` and **not** a redaction switch, so the control Secret was itself redacted; and fixtures created with the test's own field manager made the agent's restore conflict on the very field the restore exists to revert. **Three findings, none failure-driven, none fixed here (PROTOCOL §10.1):** (1) **a Secret restore never succeeds in production today** — `Sanitize` redacts every Secret with no switch, correctly, so the only Secret body a plan can carry is one the replayer must refuse, while the plan's own caveat tells the operator the material "lives in the journal store and is verified against those digests on replay"; it does not, the only unredacted copy is `execute.Snapshot.Live` and it never leaves memory. The refusal is right and the **caveat** is the wrong promise; closing it is the deferred `journal.BlobSink` work. (2) **`UndoStep.Object` has no `SHA256` field** while `PreStateSnapshot` does, so an inline body is trusted by size alone. (3) **the replayer is strictly stricter than `ValidateReplayable`** — it demands a uid pin on apply and scale, the validator only on delete — so a plan the validator blesses can be refused at replay time; the honest fix tightens the **validator** so such plans downgrade at generation, which §10.1 keeps out of this unit. **A fourth thing worth stating as a property:** a restore can only revert what the agent's own field manager owns, because `ClientApplier.Apply` does not force ownership (03 §6 — a conflict is the `contested` signal); that is correct and costs nothing in production, where a contested field never reaches execution. **`P9-T7c-3c-ii` was split at IMPLEMENT into ii-a (this unit) and ii-b (`Pager` + `Pauser`), on an invariant rather than on size:** 06 §2.2.1's broker grant is read-only on `agents` and carries no `events` verb, and V-BRK-013 asserts it exactly and is BLOCKING-ALWAYS, so a broker-side pauser cannot exist — the invariant-preserving shape is 05 §1.7's "exactly one code path that stops an agent", a controller-side C-BR reconciler, which ii-b now owns. **Explicit non-claim:** `cmd/broker/main.go` still installs `broker.UnavailablePipeline{}`, so nothing DEPLOYED reaches this replayer; [[LSN-007]] stands until P9-T7c-3d. **T7c-3c-ii-b-1 done 2026-07-28** ([#58](https://github.com/adamparco/kube-agents/pull/58), `fabbed9`) — rung 5 is now recordable, and closing a fail-open hole in the policy that guards it turned out to be the larger half of the unit.** `internal/broker/escalate` is the broker's `verify.Pager` and `verify.Pauser`. **V-REV-006 is green at L1**, its 09 §6.3 level list widened `L2` → `L1, L2` — nothing removed, relaxed or narrowed, so PROTOCOL §10.2 is satisfied; the L2 half is unchanged and still owed by ii-b-2. **The broker cannot pause anything, and that is the design, not a gap.** 06 §2.2.1 gives it `get, list, watch` on `agents` and no `events` verb at all, V-BRK-013 asserts that grant exactly and is BLOCKING-ALWAYS, and 05 §1.7 requires "exactly one code path that stops an agent". So the only pause the broker can perform is a **recorded request** on the action's own journal entry — a new `status.escalation` with the two-writer split written into the type: the broker sets `pageRequested`/`pauseRequested`/`reason`/`requestedAt`, and C-BR sets `pagedAt`/`pausedAt`/`failure` once it has done them. The pause is therefore **asynchronous**, and the package doc says so plainly rather than hiding it: that window is real and it is the price of the invariant. **`Pauser` was widened from `(agentIdentity, reason)` to a `PauseRequest`** for the reason `Rollbacker` was widened in ii-a — an implementation handed only an identity would have to re-derive, from an index, a fact its caller already had. A pause that does not name the record it belongs to cannot be written down at all. **The Get is keyed on `journal.RecordName(actionID)`, not the actionID.** An actionID is an uppercase ULID and is not a legal object name; keying on it directly would have produced a 404 that reads as "somebody deleted the record", sending whoever debugs a failed page to look for a deletion that never happened. **FINDING — a live fail-open in `config/policy/vap-agent-scope-journal.yaml`, found while adding a row to it and fixed here ([[LSN-041]]).** The policy's header comment asserted that unenumerated `status` fields were caught by a catch-all variable `unknownStatusFieldChanged`. No such variable has ever existed. Validation 1 admits any UPDATE for which `nothingChanged` holds, and `nothingChanged` conjoins only the **enumerated** fields — so the policy failed open on every field it did not know about, from **every** principal, including the human cluster-admin it exists to stop. Adding `status.escalation` under that policy would have shipped an unauthenticated stop button for any agent in the namespace, arriving with an audit trail saying the stop was deserved. Closed in three layers: `escalationChanged` joins the `nothingChanged` conjunction and each of the undo-controller / ChatOps / exporter denial conjunctions; `escalationFulfilmentSet` + a new validation 2b forbid the **owning** broker from writing the fulfilment half, because a self-attested page is worse than no record — the audit trail then asserts the promise was kept; and 8 new envtest rows prove each denial against a real API server with the shipped policy file (`TestJournalStatusPolicy`, 25 subtests, all green). **The exporter's row was deliberately not widened for C-BR** even though C-BR arrives on the same service account: the exporter is the one principal whose write unlocks deletion, so C-BR gets its own identity or nothing. That refusal is written into the policy next to the row, not just here. **Why the fix is a check and not a corrected comment.** The comment *was* the previous attempt at this fix, and it survived several reviews **because it read as protection**. `dev/tests/journal-status-vap-parity.py` (+ its negative control) is now two lines in `dev/L0-CHAIN.txt`. It reads the **Go type** rather than the generated CRD — the generated artifact is stale for the whole of the edit that adds a field, which is the only moment the check matters — and asserts parity, wiring into `nothingChanged`, that each variable reads its own field and **only** its own field, no phantoms, and non-vacuity floors. CEL cannot express the catch-all the comment described (it cannot enumerate a struct's keys, and the nearest expressible thing denies the no-op re-Update every controller does on a conflict retry), which is exactly the situation that produces a comment instead of a control. **The negative control found a hole in the check itself**: 1 of 7 mutations survived because it rewrote only the first of four CEL branches; fixed by strengthening the **check** to set-equality, not the mutation. **Evidence.** `escalate` L1: 9 tests + 2 subtests, `ok 16.041s`, 97.1% coverage. The `¬` (09 §6 line 271, mandatory) is `TestARungNeverReachedLeavesNoEscalation`, covering **both** exits that stop short of rung 5 — verification passing, and a rollback that **succeeds** — because a record claiming an escalation nobody requested is how a C-BR reconciler pauses a healthy agent; confirmed non-vacuous by mutation. The envtest half drives the **real** `verify.Driver` with the production recorder wired as both Pager and Pauser, reads `status.escalation` back **unstructured** (a fake has no schema and would pass while a real server silently pruned the field), and asserts the 512-rune bound in both directions — the recorder truncates, and the server rejects 513. Full `make -C k8s-operator test` green; full L0 chain clean. **Explicit non-claim:** nothing yet reads `status.escalation`. Until ii-b-2 ships the C-BR reconciler, a failed rollback is durably *recorded* and no agent is actually paused — the record is a promissory note, and the ledger says so rather than the check pretending otherwise. Next: **P9-T7c-3c-ii-b-2-b** (C-BR's own identity, its Deployment, and V-REV-006 at L2 with P1 in full). |

## Verification results — by check ID (09 §9.4)

One row per **check** run, keyed by its stable ID from `docs/design/09-verification-and-validation.md`
§6. Written by `harness-verify`. **The table moved to [`../../verification/results.csv`](../../verification/results.csv)
on 2026-07-26** — 37 rows moved byte-identically, 41 now, the 09 §9.4 shape it always had
(`date, phase, check_id, level, target, result, evidence_ref, notes`). It was 105 KB of the ledger and
nothing reads it during ORIENT; a CSV is the format 09 §9.4 asks for anyway.

`evidence_ref` points at the real artifact — command output, the denial message, an `ActionRecord`
ID, an audit-log query. **A `pass` with no `evidence_ref` is recorded as `skipped`, not as a pass.**
Keep the most recent result per `(check_id, level, target)`. A full run additionally emits the
machine-readable manifest at `verification/manifest-<phase>-<YYYYMMDD>.csv` with the complete 09 §9.4
field set (`requirement_ids[]`, `duration_s`, `started_at`, `image_digests[]`, `notes`).

**Two drifts are carried across rather than laundered, because normalizing them would be inventing
results.** The `result` column holds `correction` and `finding` on ten rows; 09 §9.4's enum is
`pass | fail | deferred | skipped | quarantined` and neither word is in it. Five `(check_id, level,
target)` keys appear twice, against the keep-the-most-recent rule directly above, and every row
carries the same date, so which one is most recent is not recoverable. Both are for the next full run
to write correctly, not for this move to guess at. The `target` column records `kind*` throughout:
that is what those runs actually ran on, and history does not get retconned by a substrate change.

## Deferrals

Every check that could not run, with a **named external blocker**. Deferred is a first-class result:
it is never reported as passing, and reclassifying a failure as a deferral is a named reward hack
(SELF-IMPROVEMENT §4). **A BLOCKING-ALWAYS check may not be deferred** — if it cannot run, the build
is not verifiable, and that is a halt (09 §9.6). Reviewed at every improvement pass; promote any row
whose blocker has cleared.

That is the spec's fail-closed direction (03 §6: no recoverable pre-state ⇒ no action) and not a hole; it is an availability cost, and it is invisible until someone patches a large ConfigMap or a CRD. Recorded here rather than left implicit because "the adapter is written" reads as "the path works". | human (bucket + Workload Identity), then harness | A `journal.BlobSink` implementation is provisioned and `cmd/broker` constructs `journal.NewStore(k8s, sink)` with `bodystore.Journal` behind `execute.Config.BodyStore`. Promotion now has a second, sharper test: a Secret captured through the sink and replayed from it must restore the live material, and the caveat's wording must become true rather than aspirational. |

The blocker is not the adapter. Observing whether pod A can reach service B:port from INSIDE the cluster requires a workload that can dial from A's network position: an ephemeral pod in A's namespace with A's ServiceAccount, or a standing daemonset with an exec surface. Both are new deployable objects with their own RBAC, their own NetworkPolicy posture, and their own blast-radius argument — the broker executing arbitrary dials from arbitrary namespaces is a capability 03 has to price, not a method signature to fill in. That is a **provisioning** unit, like the `journal.BlobSink` row above, and folding it into an adapter unit would have put a privileged probe pod in the middle of a Go seam. **What the gap costs today:** the connectivity row is the only one of the eight in 04 §5.1 with no working prober, so any envelope carrying a `ConnectivityProbe` expectation cannot verify and will be rolled back after its window. Until then the row is **deferred, not passing** — the L1 and L2 tests prove the absence is reported honestly, which is a different claim. |

A workflow that declares a publish step is evidence of intent, not of an artifact, and the gap between those two is exactly this row. The observable cost is that any Agent CR applied from `examples/` renders a gateway pod that sits in `ImagePullBackOff` forever; for three phases the L2 suites inherited one of those pods as ambient residue and read it as scenery, which is LSN-026 in its natural habitat. Publishing to the `gke-labs` org is a permission the harness does not hold. | human | An unauthenticated manifest fetch returns 200 for all four `ghcr.io/gke-labs/kube-agents/<name>:v0.1.0` tags. Deliberately a REGISTRY read and not a workflow read: the L0 test already proves the workflow side, and proved it green throughout the entire period every one of these tags was unpullable, so re-reading workflows can never promote this row. Promotion needs a networked check, which puts it at L2/L3 rather than in `test_image_provenance.py`, whose hermeticity is worth keeping intact. |

> **Zero open, and the number is not the point.** Six lessons were mechanized (LSN-001/002/003 by the
> L2 precondition declarations, LSN-011 by the post-merge forge audit, LSN-012 by the content-resolved
> remote preflight, LSN-014 by the §14 spec-ID lints), and building them opened three more that are
> also closed: a caller passing a flag its parser no longer has (LSN-021), `git checkout` destroying
> two hours of unstaged work during a mutation test (LSN-022), and a lint satisfied by the very
> comment it required to be present (LSN-023). **Two of the six had stood open behind a sentence that
> was true** — LSN-011's "the flag leaves no trace in the tree" (the trace is on the forge) and
> LSN-003's "enforcement is per-check, a convention not a mechanism" (a convention becomes a mechanism
> the moment something reads the declaration). A lesson called unmechanizable is usually one where the
> obvious place to look is the wrong place.

> **What the pass found in the build, not in the harness.** Three escapes and one refused deferral.
> P3-K7 had been passing `--github-cidrs` to a renderer that no longer accepts it since P8-T4:
> argparse exited 2 into `/dev/null`, the bundle was never written, and the phase3 → phase6 → phase7
> cascade went red three phases from the cause. `C-JR` and `C-AD` — both load-bearing in 05 §1 — had
> no probe row in 09 §5.1 at all, and five 06 contracts were missing from §5.2. And **V-MET-011 was
> recorded as deferred and the V-MET-006 lint refused the row**: V-MET is BLOCKING-ALWAYS, "the
> generator is not written" is not an external blocker, and the correct outcome is a scheduled task
> (P8-T10, gating the Phase 8 milestone) rather than a deferral. The lint written to catch this class
> caught the harness writing one.

> **What this pass found, and the shape of it.** Six lessons closed (LSN-035, 042, 043, 044, 045,
> 046), open lessons **6 → 1**. But the finding worth reading is a chain of three defects that were
> each hiding the next. The ledger deferred the 09 §6.14 **†** checks as a *category* — accurate
> prose, and invisible to the gate arm that hunts deferred BLOCKING-ALWAYS checks by ID, so
> **V-CTN-021 sat deferred and unasked for three phases**. Fixing that meant granting a narrow
> exemption (a check whose 09 §6 phase has not arrived is unstarted, not deferred), and an exemption
> is only safe if it expires — so it was tested at phases 9, 10, 11, 12 and unknown, expecting three
> failures. All five came back exempt: a **false pass** on `results.csv` row 47 was short-circuiting
> the arm before the exemption was reached. Appending the correction row did not clear it either,
> because the record is append-only and the reader grepped it for the word — the `**correction**`
> convention the record has followed since V-MET-014 was **decorative to every machine that read
> it**, and a retracted claim went on vouching for itself indefinitely.
>
> Three independent defects, each sufficient on its own, found in one sitting only because a
> carve-out was tested rather than argued. **A false pass is not inert** — it is an input to every
> check that asks "has this ever been green", and each of those goes quiet in a way indistinguishable
> from the property holding. Recorded as **LSN-046**.
>
> **T-9 resolved** (per-kind settle windows published in 04 §5.1), which is the first §12 tightening
> the harness has closed. It ratifies numbers the implementation already committed to rather than
> inventing any, which is the only form 09 §12's preamble permits. **T-6 is now on a deadline that
> enforces itself:** the exemption keeping V-CTN-021 legal lapses at phase 11 with no edit to
> anything, so the spec work has to land before Phase 11 opens or the build goes red on its own.


> **What this pass mechanized, and the one it found by accident.** Four lessons closed. LSN-050 got
> `dev/tests/gitcorpus.py` — one `--cached --others --exclude-standard` enumerator, now the only way
> ten L0 checks learn what files exist — plus `check_l0_corpus_is_not_index_only`, which **AST-parses**
> every `.py` and `.sh` under `dev/` and fails any `ls-files` argv missing `--others`. The AST is not
> fastidiousness: `gitcorpus.py`, the gate arm itself and seven converted docstrings all discuss
> `git ls-files --others` in prose, and a grep cannot tell the sentence from the argv ([[LSN-023]]).
> The arm scans the whole tree rather than the chain, because the lesson's own words are "the eighth
> script written next month copies the seventh" — a rule that binds only once a script reaches
> `L0-CHAIN.txt` catches the defect after it is written, reviewed and merged.
>
> **LSN-047, LSN-048 and LSN-049 got one home, not three,** because they are one lesson: the sweep
> scored an exit code it had not established was the test suite's. `dev/mutate.py` refuses to produce
> a number it cannot back — no `-run` filter, every row naming the test that must fail, an applier
> that refuses a needle it does not find exactly once (which is also how it observes the mutation
> LANDED), and a third verdict, `BROKEN`, for a mutant it could not evaluate, so the denominator
> cannot silently shrink. The half `dev/mutate.sh` could never supply is the routing: `harness-run`
> §5 and `harness-verify` §3 now say a sweep is **configured, not authored**, which is the
> [[LSN-019]] shape those three lessons kept recurring through — a mechanization off the path the
> work takes is not a mechanization.
>
> **`BROKEN` is a third verdict and not a finding.** That is LSN-048's real content: a false red
> recommending a plausible action (go strengthen the test) is worse than one that wastes time,
> because the "fix" passes on the first run and the mutant stays unmeasured.
>
> **The accident.** Checking the four bodies against the index turned up LSN-044's body saying `open`
> where its index row said `closed` — the stale header behind the miscount that triggered the pass.
> The count lives in three places in one file (index column, body header, `**Open: N of M**` tally),
> all hand-edited, and it is what `harness-run` §2 reads to decide whether the next invocation is an
> improvement pass and nothing else. `check_lesson_status_matches_its_index_row` makes the other two
> agree with the index, including the IDs the tally names. A body with no header still passes: 32 of
> 50 have never carried one, and requiring it everywhere would add 32 more copies of the value the
> check exists to stop duplicating.
>
> Reconciling the ledger's own copy then found a second, quieter one. Nine rows of **Lessons opened /
> closed** still read `**open**` for lessons closed phases ago, and the metrics table's P9-T7c-4a row
> had been written with **four cells instead of nine** — escape rate present, open lessons and
> deferrals and coverage simply absent. A short markdown row is legal markdown; it renders, and the
> missing cells read as "not measured". `check_metrics_rows_are_complete` now counts them, ignoring
> `\|`, which is how it immediately found a **tenth** cell in the P9-T7d-5 row: an unescaped
> `envsubst | kubectl apply -f -` inside a code span had been splitting that row for a day.
>
> **One deferral reclassified, none promoted.** 06 §1.2's **V-11** had sat as a deferral since
> 2026-07-27 with the blocker "the check itself is missing". A missing check is unstarted work, not
> an external obstruction — the ruling V-MET-011 got in Phase 8 and V-G1..V-G4 got four days ago.
> Both halves are now scheduled: **V-CTR-019** (09 §6.9, L2, `¬`) and **P10-T8** (07 §2). Phase 10
> rather than 9, because that is where `allowedUsers` first decides something, and because the
> not-yet-due clause of `check_dagger_checks_are_deferred_by_id` then gives the work a deadline that
> expires on its own. The row is deliberately **not** marked CLOSED: nothing runs yet, and
> `_closed_deferral_failures` is right to demand an artifact that does.
>
> **Pruned: nothing, and the criterion is why.** Archival takes a mechanization that has held three
> phases or more. Every lesson here was seeded or opened in Phase 8 or 9, so that set is still empty
> — the same answer as the last two passes, and it starts selecting at the Phase 10 milestone.
>
> **Refusals: none.** Every open lesson this pass considered was mechanizable. LSN-040 stays open by
> rule, not by argument — its fix is code (**P9-T7c-4b** / **V-BRK-022**) and §5 forbids
> implementation during a pass.

## Lessons opened / closed

The store is `.claude/harness/LESSONS.md`; this is the pointer and the running count. An **open
lesson is a defect in the harness**. Over the `binding.md` threshold (**5**), the next invocation is
an improvement pass and nothing else. A lesson open across three passes escalates to a human.

| Date | Lesson | Opened by | Status | Mechanization |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2026-07-29 | **LSN-050** | P9-T7c-3d-iv-a CHECKPOINT — the full L0 chain printed nothing, and CI failed on the very check that exists for the defect | **closed** (improvement pass 2026-07-29 — `dev/tests/gitcorpus.py` + `check_l0_corpus_is_not_index_only`) | **The pre-commit gate cannot see a file that has not been committed.** A new test file's fake API-server error string named `agents.kubeagents.io`; the operator serves `kubeagents.x-k8s.io`, and `dev/tests/api-group-single-sourced.py` exists for exactly that ([[LSN-032]]) and is on the L0 chain. It ran, scanned 115 files, and passed — over a corpus that did not contain the new file, because `git ls-files` without `--others` lists the **index**, and the file was still `??`. **Seven L0 scripts share the defect**: `api-group-single-sourced.py`, `cli-contract.py`, `install-artifacts-are-rendered.py`, `install-render-is-faithful.py`, `one-broker-per-agent.py`, `invariants-gate.py`, `scope-label-single-sourced.py`. Worse than an ordinary gap because the blindness is **perfectly correlated with novelty** — the checks are weakest on code nothing has ever reviewed — and because it is **self-concealing**: the correct habit (run the chain, then stage, then commit) means any unit that happens to re-run the chain after `git add` sees the check work. **Mechanization:** one shared `ls-files -z --cached --others --exclude-standard` helper across all seven, plus a gate check that no L0 script may call `ls-files` without `--others` — without the second, the helper is a convention and the eighth script copies the seventh. Expect the first run to surface real findings in files untracked across several units. Not fixed here: seven call sites plus a corpus change with its own verification surface, and PROTOCOL §10 forbids a check change in the unit that motivated it. |
| 2026-07-29 | **LSN-049** | P9-T8a VERIFY — the sweep reported row 14 as ESCAPED, twice, on a property the suite catches cleanly | **closed** (improvement pass 2026-07-29 — `dev/mutate.py`; needles never cross a shell parse) | **The sweep's own shell quoting invented a hole, and `rc == 0` called it a result.** Row 14's needle contains `""` — Go's empty string literal, because the mutated line is `return false, false, ""`. The sweep interpolated needles and replacements into a **double-quoted `bash -c` argument**, so the embedded quote closed the string early, the applier died before touching the file, the `&&` short-circuited, and the surrounding `dev/mutate.sh` still exited **0** — which the sweep read as "the suite passed with the mutation in place". **[[LSN-048]] with the sign flipped, and the flip does not help.** There a `-run` pattern matching nothing exited 0 and hid a hole; here a shell parse failure exited 0 and invented one. Both reduce to the same root: **the sweep scored an exit code it had not established was the test suite's.** `rc == 0` is load-bearing and is produced by a pipeline of things that are not the test suite — a `-run` filter, a shell parse, an applier, an `&&` — any of which can hand back a 0 meaning "I did nothing". The invented-hole direction is not the safe one: it cost two passes here, and a lazy investigation terminates in a **weakened property**, because the natural move on a mutation that allegedly survives is to relax what you thought you were asserting. **What caught it:** requiring each row to name the *specific* test that must appear in the failing set rather than accepting "something went red" — the same requirement had already caught a mis-attribution on the same row (the intuitive guess was `TestNothingComposesBackToExecuting`; the real catcher is `TestAnUnobservableAgentIsShadowed`). A sweep scoring on `rc != 0` goes green on both defects. **Mechanization:** three properties in the same sanctioned-sweep change LSN-047 and LSN-048 already wait on — mutation text never crosses a shell parse (needle and replacement travel by environment or file to an applier that **refuses unless the target appears exactly once**, which also turns a stale needle into `BROKEN` rather than a silent escape); the applier's failure must be distinguishable from the suite's success, so `&&` is not enough and the sweep must observe the mutation landed before scoring; and each row declares its catching test. **Nothing here is `dev/mutate.sh`'s fault** — it restored byte-perfectly through all 15 rows as it did through LSN-048's eight. All three are about the layer above it that every unit re-authors from scratch. **Three re-earnings is the argument.** **Open lessons: 4 of 49** (LSN-040, LSN-047, LSN-048, LSN-049; below the threshold of 5). |
| 2026-07-29 | **LSN-048** | P9-T7c-3d-ii-a VERIFY — the mutation sweep came back 5/8 with three survivors, and all three were the sweep naming a test that does not exist | **closed** (improvement pass 2026-07-29 — `dev/mutate.py`; catchers verified before the first mutation) | **A sweep that cannot find its own test reports the mutation as SURVIVED.** `go test -run 'TestBrakeFailClosed'` against a package whose table test is actually called `TestBrakeEachRuleFiresInIsolation` matches nothing, prints `no tests to run`, and **exits 0** — so the composing idiom `dev/mutate.sh f -- sh -c 'mutate && ! check'` sees `! 0` = false and scores the mutation uncaught. **The direction of the lie is what makes it expensive.** A sweep that falsely reported CAUGHT would be a silent false green, and this repo has checks for that shape. This one falsely reports a **hole**, which reads as a finding — and the natural response to a finding is to go write a test for it. That test would pass immediately (the property is already covered), it would look like the fix, and the three mutations would still never have been evaluated. The sweep's verdict on them is *unknown*, presented as *known*. Two of the three here were `IsUndo() -> true`, which exempts every action from pause and freeze, and a row 7 that refuses without escalating — both genuinely caught once the pattern resolved. **Class:** [[LSN-035]] applied to the harness rather than to a check — an operation that verifies it *ran* rather than that it *worked*; and a near neighbour of [[LSN-038]], where a predicate that can only make its caller stricter is the one nobody writes a negative control for. Here the predicate can only make the sweep look *worse*, which is why it survives review just as easily. **Mechanization:** a `go test -list` guard before each mutation — if the pattern selects zero tests the sweep prints `BROKEN SWEEP` and scores it as neither caught nor survived. Used for this unit's 8/8 and not yet durable. It belongs in the same artifact as LSN-047 (`dev/mutate.sh` cannot see the `-run` pattern, so the enforceable form is the `harness-run` §5 skill change that makes a sweep configured rather than authored), and the two should land together. **Open lessons: 3 of 48** (LSN-040, LSN-047, LSN-048; below the threshold of 5) — superseded by the LSN-049 row above. |
| 2026-07-29 | **LSN-047** | P9-T7c-3c-iii — the throwaway mutation harness backed both files up under one name and restored the wrong one over the other, destroying an untracked source file mid-sweep | **closed** (improvement pass 2026-07-29 — `dev/mutate.py`; snapshots keyed by position, and the skills route to it) | **A near-miss that only looked like a scripting slip.** The sweep snapshotted its two targets into `BAK / f.name`; both are called `cooldown.go` (`internal/broker/cooldown/` and `internal/broker/verify/`), so the second copy clobbered the first and the `finally` restore then wrote `verify`'s contents over **both** paths. The first run had already reported `12/13 caught` and exited 0 — it ran against intact sources and did the damage on the way out — so the failure was invisible until the second run came back `2/13` with eleven "anchor not found" lines. The file was untracked, so git could not restore it; it was rewritten from context with every subsequent edit reapplied, and the re-swept result is `13/13` with both sources byte-identical to their backups. **The lesson is not "use unique backup names".** `dev/mutate.sh` already exists, already snapshots by index rather than by basename, and would not have had this bug — and nothing in `harness-run` §5 routes a mutation sweep to it, so each unit writes a fresh throwaway that re-derives the same mechanics and re-earns the same mistakes. That is [[LSN-019]]'s shape one level over: the sanctioned artifact exists, and the ritual that should reach for it does not name it. **Candidate mechanization:** a `harness-run` §5 skill change making `dev/mutate.sh` the sweep path, so a sweep is configured rather than authored. Deferred out of this unit deliberately — a skill edit is `harness-improve`'s business, not a feature unit's. **Open lessons: 2 of 47** (LSN-040, LSN-047; below the threshold of 5). |

| 2026-07-28 | **LSN-040** | P9-T7c-1 — assembling steps 3-11 and driving one real envelope through them; the first happy-path fixture (`apply` a ConfigMap) was refused at step 9 by an integrity check saying the classifier had been shown no changed fields | **closed** 2026-07-29 (P9-T7c-4b — `k8s-operator/internal/broker/pipeline/verbs_test.go`, **V-BRK-022** at L1, run by `Run Controller Tests`; sweep 15/15) | **Two packages, each right, about the same word.** `classify.Resolve` sets `WholeObject` for `create`, `apply` **and** `delete` — correct, because to a rule all three touch every field and there is no path list to reason about. `execute.CheckIntegrity` accepts `WholeObject` for `create` and `delete` **only** and its `default:` arm rejects the rest — also correct, because an `apply` has a computed diff and accepting "everything changed" would let a change pass the integrity check with no path compared; `execute`'s own `TestIntegrityWholeObjectIsNotAnEscapeHatch` asserts that reading deliberately. What was missing is the conversion between them, which did not exist because nothing had ever called one with the other's output. **This is a different class from [[LSN-007]]**, which it superficially resembles: LSN-007 is one component with no caller, this is two components each with callers and tests, which agree on a type signature and disagree on what a field of it means — no check on either package could have found it, because each package's tests assert its own reading and both readings are right. It is findable only by the first thing that puts them in a line, so the mechanization has to be at the seam. **Consequence:** only `create`, `delete` and JSON-patch `patch` traverse the pipeline today; `apply`, `scale` and merge-patch **fail closed** at step 9, so this is missing functionality and not a hole. Pinned as a property with a verdict rather than a comment — `TestApplyFailsClosedAtTheIntegrityCheck` — so the next reader finds a test, not a surprise. **One level down**, `classify.RawOp.Patch` is documented as carrying "the RFC 6902 patch for `patch`, or the computed diff for `apply`" and `pipeline.rawOps` only fills it for the JSON Patch media type, so an `apply` was also being **classified** with no `TouchedPaths` and no per-path direction analysis — fail-closed saved it, and the classification was the quieter defect. **Planned mechanization (P9-T7c-4):** supply the computed diff for `apply` and `/spec/replicas` for `scale`, derive merge-patch paths, and then the part that is the lesson rather than the bug — a check that **every verb in the envelope's closed verb enum executes end to end**, discovered from the enum rather than from a list ([[LSN-036]]), because a table covering the three verbs that happen to work would have printed green throughout the entire period the other three did not. **Open lessons: 2 of 40** (LSN-035, LSN-040; below the threshold of 5). |

Its docstring says so outright: _"Deliberately NOT checked: that a step does the right thing. This is reachability only."_ Reachability of scripts. The manifests were never in the graph. `common.sh:656` had already written the same finding down for a different pair of files — "Both manifests existed in examples/gitops-repo/ from Phase 3 and NO INSTALL PATH APPLIED EITHER — the same defect class as the egress policies (LSN-006/LSN-007)" — fixed those two by rendering them from `common.sh`, and did not generalize; so the class has now been paid for **three times** (egress policies, tenant quota + default-deny, every agent identity). Generalized: **a closed lesson is closed against an instance, and the next instance arrives one edge over, same class, different node type.** The tell is a check whose docstring narrows its own claim — every such sentence is honest, and collectively they map where the class is still free to recur. Aggravated here because the exemplar tree does not *look* inert: version-controlled, prettier-formatted, named in 06 §2 line 455, read by five `verify-phase*.sh` suites, applied **selectively** by `dev/cluster/up.sh` and `provision_03`, and as of this unit checked by V-BRK-013 — partial application means "is this tree applied?" answers *yes, some of it*, and no reader can tell which. **Closed in P9-T7d-5 by V-CMP-007** (`dev/tests/identity-has-install-path.py`, on L0-CHAIN), and NOT in the planned form. The plan was a sixth property in `install-path-wired.py` over the exemplar tree; what shipped is a separate check over the **install path** (`k8s-operator/scripts/`), because the property that makes an identity real is not “is this exemplar inert?” but “does every identity the broker references get created by a step someone runs?” — the exemplar tree could be deleted entirely and the broker pod would still not start. Seven properties, 8 negative controls, the load-bearing one being LSN-039 itself reproduced: one tier's identity stops being applied while the others keep working. **The finding as first written was too broad and is corrected here.** _“No `provision_NN_*.sh` step creates any agent ServiceAccount, Role or RoleBinding”_ came from a grep over `*.sh`; the identities are created from `.yaml.template` files piped through `envsubst | kubectl apply -f -`. A read-only sweep of the live cluster narrowed it to three claims and proved all three: the cluster-admin and developer-team **reader** SAs were created imperatively; the **platform** reader SA was created by nothing (a bare hand-applied object, no labels in its `last-applied-configuration`, its Workload Identity annotation added by a separate hand `kubectl annotate`); and no actor SA and no broker-operations grant existed on any install path at all. Both versions motivate the same unit and the same mechanization, which is exactly why the wide one survived four artifacts — **a finding stated one generalization wider than the evidence is a claim the next reader cannot reproduce**, and the reader who tries and fails learns to discount the finding rather than to narrow it. **Still owed, and routed rather than dropped:** part (d) of the plan — the declare-or-fail table over `examples/gitops-repo/` — belongs to the queued `managed-by: gitops` sweep, the unit that touches that tree. **Open lessons: 1 of 39** (LSN-035) at the time this row was written; **2 of 40** as of LSN-040. |

| 2026-07-27 | **LSN-035** | P9-T5b — a mutation survived, and the rule it broke turned out to be one no input can reach | **closed** (mechanized — `dev/tests/negative-controls-name-their-rule.py`) | Mutation-testing the ¬ negative controls for V-PRO-021 killed 9 of 11 invariants; the 2 survivors were **the two properties the check text names by hand**. Not missing tests — both rules had tests and both passed for an unrelated reason, because every history written to enter rung 2 twice had to *descend* to do it and the non-decreasing rule rejected it first. **A test that asserts "this is rejected" cannot tell you which rule did the rejecting.** Deeper: within a chain-valid history the two rules are **logically unreachable** — monotonicity plus no-self-transition already imply both — so no better history exists to write. The general finding is that a **redundant** guard and an **unenforced** guard are indistinguishable from a green suite, and mutation testing reports them identically as a survivor; a survivor is therefore a question (*is this rule reachable?*) whose two answers need opposite responses, and "add a test for the surviving rule" answers neither. Where `¬` requires a negative control, that control only ever proves the **suite** fails, never **which rule** made it fail — so where rules overlap, the narrow ones silently stop carrying their weight. **Not closed here.** The ladder was repaired by moving assertions off the rules and onto the properties (`TestLadderPropertiesHoldOverEveryAcceptedHistory`, all 1554 histories of length ≤ 4, accepted count pinned at exactly 30, re-mutated to confirm it is what now kills monotonicity), and both derived rules were **kept** with the finding written into `ladder.go` — the implication runs one way, and a rule deleted for redundancy is one nobody restores when the premise changes. But exhaustive enumeration only worked because the state space is tiny, so it is not the general mechanization. Candidates for the next `harness-improve`: require every ¬ check to record *which* rule its negative control exercised and assert the error names it, or make reachability an explicit written question a survivor must answer before it may be allowlisted. Sibling of [[lsn-032]] and [[lsn-033]] — **a check that shares a premise with the thing it checks cannot see a defect in the premise**. |

## Decisions & deviations

When a spec is genuinely silent and the harness picks an option, record it here (README rule #3).
This is what a reviewer reads to understand choices the specs didn't dictate. **Phases 0–7 are in
[`archive/LEDGER-phases-0-7.md`](archive/LEDGER-phases-0-7.md);** below is Phase 8 and the two
phase-independent rows.

| Date | Phase | Decision | Rationale | Spec touched |

| 2026-07-30 | 9 | Step 3's live-read failures are typed by **whether retrying could ever help**, not by which read failed — `403 target-forbidden` (no Retry-After) for an RBAC denial or a rejected credential, `503 snapshot-failed` (with one) for anything else | 06 §4.4 requires a refusal and does not name it. The two failures are indistinguishable in the error and opposite in the remedy: one clears by itself, one never does. A caller told to wait sixty seconds and retry a permission boundary loops forever, which `Refusal.RetryAfterSeconds` already forbids in prose ("zero means do not retry, which is the right answer for every schema and authorization refusal") and which this site was the last one violating. `ReasonSnapshotFailed` already existed for the persist half at brake row 4 and had never been wired for the capture half. | 09 §6.2 — new **V-BRK-031** |
| 2026-07-30 | 9 | The `target-forbidden` arm **journals and does not raise a security event** | 03 §6's security events are identity violations — a caller that is not who it says it is — and `forbidden-caller` (V-BRK-010) remains that case. This is an authorization outcome for a correctly _authenticated_ caller, and in shadow mode the actor holds no tenant authority at all, so it fires on every single action: an alarm on everything is an alarm that gets muted, and the cost lands on the events that matter. The journal still records it, which is what makes a probing pattern findable by analysis afterwards — and recording it _somewhere_ is the half of the defect that mattered most, since `Journal` rides on the `Refusal` and an untyped error was journaled nowhere at all. | — |
| 2026-07-30 | 9 | `broker-auth-l2.sh`'s L2-0 baseline arm discriminates on the **reason**, not the status | `forbidden-caller` and `target-forbidden` are two 403s about two different subjects: the identity presenting the credential, and the identity the broker acts as. A status-only arm would have gone red on a broker doing exactly the right thing — halt condition 2. **Guardrail 9 does not bite**: the arm was _passing_ the 500 with a NOTE, so this is not a check edited so a failing implementation passes. The amendment is a strict narrowing — every reason that failed before still fails, one previously-impossible reason is named, and one of the five new `¬` rows is "a genuine auth refusal is still a failure" so the narrowing cannot swallow the case the arm existed for. | — |
| 2026-07-30 | 9 | The broker's image is set on the CONTROLLER, and `deploy_broker` waits for the rendered brokers to converge on it — not for the controller's rollout | There is no `deploy/kubeagents-broker` to `set image` on, by design: the operator renders one broker per Agent CR and reads the image off its own environment, because naming the broker's image chooses the binary behind the actor credential, which is the same authority-choosing move 06 §2.2.1 forbids for the actor ServiceAccount itself. That indirection means the obvious wait is the wrong one. `rollout status` on the controller proves the controller restarted; it says nothing about whether a single broker Deployment has been re-rendered, and a suite that started there would assert P1 against brokers still carrying the previous digest. So there are two waits and the second is the claim. It also produces a distinct exit code: **rc 5** (the digest is deployed but the workload did not come up) is a different answer from rc 4 (the image did not materialise), and collapsing them would report a cluster-config problem as a build failure. | 06 §2.2.1 (read, not changed) |
